In an unsymmetrical pinacol rearrangement:

1. Water leaves preferentially from the carbon that gives the more stable carbocation.
2. The group on the adjacent carbon with greater migratory aptitude then shifts as the remaining hydroxyl group becomes the carbonyl.
3. Electron-rich aryl groups migrate better than phenyl or alkyl groups; ethyl migrates better than methyl.

### Compound A
Loss of water from the phenyl-bearing carbon gives the more stable benzylic carbocation. Ethyl, rather than methyl, migrates from the adjacent carbon:

\[
\ce{CH3CO-C(Ph)(CH2CH3)2}
\]

Thus,

\[
A=\text{3-ethyl-3-phenylpentan-2-one}
\]

### Compound B
The carbocation stabilized by the 4-hydroxyphenyl group is favored. Phenyl migrates in preference to methyl, giving:

\[
B=\text{3-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-3-phenylpentan-2-one}
\]

### Compound C
Let \(\mathrm{An}=4\)-methoxyphenyl. Water loss from the carbon bearing two anisyl groups gives the more stable carbocation. From the adjacent carbon, an electron-rich anisyl group migrates preferentially over phenyl:

\[
\ce{PhCO-C(An)3}
\]

Therefore,

\[
C=\text{2,2,2-tris(4-methoxyphenyl)-1-phenylethan-1-one}
\]

These three products correspond to option D. The alternative A and B structures in the other options also fail carbon conservation.

Answer: D
